text: We asked the Lord to heal him. He took him home instead. The grief is ours to carry now, not his.
speaker: Stephen

text: His daughter comes, and three grandsons who stand very still in the doorway.
Of dying? A little. Of what comes after? Not since Pentecost.
speaker: Yosef

text: He takes your hand. His grip is still strong from sixty years at the wheel.
What do you do for him?
There is no miracle in the room. There is no fear in it either.
Yosef dies a little before dawn, with his daughter’s hand in his and your scroll on the blanket.
Yosef heard Peter at Pentecost and was baptized at eighty. Now he is dying, and he has asked for “the scribe who writes things down.”
Yosef heard Peter at Pentecost and was baptized at eighty. Now he is dying, and he has asked for “the girl who writes things down.”
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies. Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
